messages:
maya: FYI ticket #12487 from acme-payments — they report intermittent signature verification failures for tokens signed by our KMS proxy using CloudHSM. Failures only on ~0.5-1% of requests, all from a single region.
acme-payments: attaching minimal repro and logs, sig verification sometimes returns 'invalid signature' downstream. We see the signed payload is shorter by a few bytes when failure occurs.
maya: Got the repro, thanks. Collecting customer logs now. Initial hypothesis: network truncation (MTU/path), client library bug, or HSM firmware oddity.
jonathan: Could be client-side chunking. Which CloudHSM client version and HSM firmware? Also, do they use TLS termination at proxy or passthrough?
acme-payments: cloudhsm-client v2.9.1, HSM firmware 3.2.5, we terminate TLS at the KMS proxy (our side).
lee: Any relevant errors in system logs or tcp retransmits? If packets are being dropped we might see RSTs or partial writes. Ask them for packet capture around a failing request.
maya: Requested pcap and full HSM audit logs. Also asked them to toggle client debug and produce base64 of the raw signed blob for a failing/working pair.
acme-payments: uploaded pcap (link), and two base64 signed blobs (one valid, one invalid). Packet capture shows a 'PSH' followed by 'FIN' in same sequence for the failing connection.
jonathan: Interesting — PSH+FIN could indicate the app closed socket mid-stream. If the app closes before full write, the HSM proxy might process truncated payload. Can we reproduce by forcibly reducing MTU or by adding a small sleep between writes?
maya: Customer willing to run test. Asked them to run this small Node script to stress sign with controlled write behavior:
```
const net = require('net');
// pseudo-repro: open TCP, write header, optionally sleep, write body
// run against KMS proxy and look for failures
```
acme-payments: ran test with a 10ms delay between chunks — failure rate dropped to near 0. Does this point to our KMS proxy not handling partial writes correctly?
jonathan: Likely. Our proxy should buffer until full message is received. Need to confirm boundary/length parsing code. Assigning to eng-crypto to validate. @lee can you verify kernel-level socket options and Nagle interactions?
lee: Will check. Also confirm if proxy uses TCP_CORK/TCP_NODELAY. Those change segmentation. If KMS proxy reads once and treats EOF as end-of-message that would cause truncation on fast-close.
pat: From security/compliance side — if truncated payloads resulted in partially processed signatures recorded as successful in audit logs, we need to flag this as an integrity risk. We should treat affected keys as potentially compromised for the incident timeline and prepare rotation guidance for the customer.
maya: Noted, patched the ticket with suggested immediate mitigation: 1) enable request validation at proxy (length-prefix checks), 2) temporarily throttle aggressive clients, 3) rotate impacted signing keys after a confirmed window.
jonathan: I've reproduced locally by writing a short program that writes the TLV header then closes socket. Found code path in kms-proxy v1.12 where read loop treats read==0 as message termination instead of continuing until length satisfied. Preparing PR.
maya: Excellent. Customer asked whether on-prem HSM customers could be affected similarly.
jonathan: Any deployment using our KMS proxy code (hosted/dedicated/private with proxy enabled) and terminating TLS at the proxy could be affected. On-prem setups that use a direct HSM client without our proxy are likely unaffected, but recommend they verify their client library behavior.
lee: I'll run a quick grep across infra images for tcp options and proxy versions. Also will add an Env check to detect socket half-close patterns and log them as WARN.
pat: For compliance, preserve audit logs as-is and attach a timeline. Don't sanitize or truncate logs. We'll need to coordinate an advisory and key rotation plan.
maya: Escalating to vendor as well — aws-cloudhsm-bot can you pull any known CloudHSM firmware issues for 3.2.5 related to partial writes?
aws-cloudhsm-bot: No known firmware bugs matching partial write behavior on 3.2.5. Recommended: review client usage patterns and proxy buffering.
acme-payments: Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll hold on rotation until you confirm scope. Also asked if billing will be affected by reissuing tokens.
maya: We'll separate billing question into ticket note; likely not — rotations are operational. Next steps: jonathan to open PR with fix and hotfix patch to proxy (priority P1), lee to produce monitoring for half-close patterns, pat to draft customer advisory and rotation checklist.
jonathan: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/kms-proxy/pull/459 — includes length-prefix enforcement and unit tests for partial writes. Requesting hotfix merge and rollout to staging.
lee: Deploying hotfix to staging now, will run customer repro harness.
maya: Setting customer expectation: we should have a staging release validated within 4 hours and a production hotfix by EOD if tests pass.
pat: Preparing compliance advisory and suggested reg notice.
acme-payments: Running our full acceptance suite against staging harness now, will report within 2 hours.
jonathan: Thanks all. After prod rollout we'll coordinate a controlled key rotation window and provide script to the customer to re-sign tokens if needed.
maya: Closing loop in ticket; will update with timestamps and links to PR/deploy logs. :thumbsup:
